grades.quote: The procedures for investigating and responding to a Report are set out in B.401.1 – Sexual Violence Procedure.

Any Member of the University Community who has experienced Sexual Violence can access confidential assistance and support, accommodations, referrals and information from the Office of Student Affairs or Human Resources regardless of the time or place at which the Sexual Violence occurred.

All Survivors have the right to pursue criminal and/or civil legal remedies and exercise any other legal rights they may have, including the right to file a complaint with the BC Human Rights Tribunal, whether or not they choose to make a Report under this Policy.

Survivors will not be discriminated against if they have engaged in illegal activities or perceived illegal activities that do not pertain to the Sexual Violence incident disclosed, such as sex work or illegal substance use.
Timeliness of investigation and response will vary based on factors including the availability of witnesses or evidence and/or involvement in other investigations and legal proceedings.
The University may impose or facilitate appropriate interim measures for the safety of the individuals involved and the University community.
“University-related Activity” includes an activity or event conducted under the authority of the University at any location, on or off campus including online forum.

The Complainant has the right to know the outcome of the investigation, but not the details of any sanctions that may have been applied to the Respondent unless sharing that information is necessary for the protection of the Complainant’s health or safety;

A public annual report including the annual budget assigned to Sexual Violence prevention and response will be produced by the Office of Student Affairs in collaboration with Human Resources and the Capilano Students’ Union (CSU).
In accordance with the Sexual Violence and Misconduct Policy Act this Policy will be reviewed every three years or when directed to by the Ministry.
A Sexual Violence Advisory Commitee has been established under this policy, made up of Members of the University Community including Students, Employees and community based partners.

Members of the University Community who are responsible for formally receiving Disclosures, Reports, conducting investigations, or making outcome decisions or responding to appeals, will receive specialized training.

The Office of Student Affairs and Human Resources will work in collaboration with the Capilano Student’s Union (CSU) and other on- and off-campus partners to implement an education and prevention plan that is based on evidence informed approaches, research, and subject mater advice.
